introduction_markdown:
**GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD - General Certificate of Education Examination. JUNE 2025, ADVANCED LEVEL. English Language, Paper 2 (0730).**

Answer your questions either exclusively from **PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS)** or from **PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS)**.

**PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS) - Duration: Two and a Quarter Hours.** Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ONE QUESTION FROM EACH SECTION (Section A: Composition, Section B: Prescribed Texts, Section C: Creative Writing). ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you no marks.

**PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS) - Duration: Three Hours.** Instructions to candidates: Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you little or no marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you little or no marks.
enonce_intro_markdown: **PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS) - SECTION A: SUMMARY AND TEXT RECONSTRUCTION (30 Marks)**
incertitudes: Consigne de la page de garde (règle de choix) : le candidat répond « exclusivement » soit à la PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS, 2h15) soit à la PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS, 3h). Le format regles_choix ne sait pas exprimer ce choix entre deux parties : il reste dans introduction_markdown. Part One : « Answer ONE question from each section » (sections A, B, C) ; Part Two : « Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C ». Les regles_choix sont identiques dans les 24 fichiers : NEW SYLLABUS - SECTION A 1 sur 6, SECTION B 1 sur 4, SECTION C 1 sur 2 ; OLD SYLLABUS - SECTION B 1 sur 6, SECTION C 1 sur 4 ; la Section A de la Part Two est obligatoire (aucune règle).

Convention de numérotation (sujet à deux parties) : numero_exercice « NEW-A1 » à « NEW-A6 », « NEW-B1 » à « NEW-B4 », « NEW-C1 » et « NEW-C2 » pour la Part One ; « OLD-A1 » et « OLD-A2 », « OLD-B1 » à « OLD-B6 », « OLD-C1 » à « OLD-C4 » pour la Part Two. duree_epreuve vaut « 3h » partout (durée de la Part Two, la plus longue) ; la Part One dure 2h15 (voir introduction_markdown).

Texte à corriger recopié tel qu'imprimé, avec ses fautes. Le sujet ne donne ni le nombre de fautes ni la répartition des 15 points : 29 corrections sont retenues par le corrigé (liste établie par moi, deux corrections étant discutables : « do not plan » devenu « did not plan », et « evolved in day » corrigé en « passed during the day », l'expression originale d'auteur n'étant pas connue). Le compte de 29 fautes est fait par script ; la grille de 0,5 point par faute est une hypothèse.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**QUESTION 2: Text Reconstruction (15 Marks)**

Read the following text, identify the mistakes in it and correct them. Then, copy the corrected text in your answer booklet, underlining all the identified and corrected mistakes.

When my daughter break the news to me over the phone application viber that my mother was taking his last breathe, I was shattered. Eventhough my mother had struggled with colon cancer and was in excruciating pain the news stroke me like an axe on my head. Immediately, I felt drained of every ounce of vitality. I felt like my heart leapt out of my chest. I had to sit down to stop me from slumping on the floor.

I do not plan to write about grief, but I taught it will be helpful to shear my experience. I belief putting my feelings on paper will bring some closure to my grief or by my sharing may help someone else.

In the immediate aftermath of the announcement, and as the hours evolved in day, I couldn't eat; I felt physical pain all over and was physically exausted.

Dealing with dead is the hard thing I ever have to deal with in my life. There is no formular or timeline for dealing with grief. The range of emotions is overwhelmed and at first I am not sure how I was supposed to react or how I was supposed to say to anyone. I was emotionally unmoored, adrifted in the wreckage of loss love, loose life and my own seeming shattered identity. This powerless, I guess, reflect the uncertainty of death.

Adapted from Profiles International; Issued 41-January/February 2016
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reconstructed text (the corrections are in bold, with the number of the fault; 29 faults)**

When my daughter **broke** (1) the news to me over the phone application **Viber** (2) that my mother was taking **her** (3) last **breath** (4), I was shattered. **Even though** (5) my mother had struggled with colon cancer and was in excruciating pain**,** (6) the news **struck** (7) me like an axe on my head. Immediately, I felt drained of every ounce of vitality. I felt like my heart leapt out of my chest. I had to sit down to stop **myself** (8) from slumping on the floor.

I **did** (9) not plan to write about grief, but I **thought** (10) it **would** (11) be helpful to **share** (12) my experience. I **believe** (13) putting my feelings on paper will bring some closure to my grief **and that** (14) my sharing may help someone else.

In the immediate aftermath of the announcement, and as the hours **passed** (15) **during the day** (16), I couldn't eat; I felt physical pain all over and was physically **exhausted** (17).

Dealing with **death** (18) is the **hardest** (19) thing I **have ever had** (20) to deal with in my life. There is no **formula** (21) or timeline for dealing with grief. The range of emotions is **overwhelming** (22) and at first I **was** (23) not sure how I was supposed to react or **what** (24) I was supposed to say to anyone. I was emotionally unmoored, **adrift** (25) in the wreckage of **lost** (26) love, **lost** (27) life and my own seeming shattered identity. This **powerlessness** (28), I guess, **reflects** (29) the uncertainty of death.

**Faults, corrections and rules**

| No. | Printed | Correction | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | break | broke | Past simple: the news was broken at a past moment, consistent with 'was shattered'. |
| 2 | viber | Viber | The name of an application is a proper noun: capital letter. |
| 3 | his | her | The possessive must agree with 'my mother' (female). |
| 4 | breathe | breath | 'Breath' is the noun (to take a last breath); 'breathe' is the verb. |
| 5 | Eventhough | Even though | A conjunction written as two words. |
| 6 | pain the news | pain, the news | A comma closes the introductory subordinate clause. |
| 7 | stroke | struck | Past simple of 'to strike' is 'struck'; 'stroke' is a noun or the base form. |
| 8 | stop me | stop myself | Reflexive pronoun when the subject and the object are the same person. |
| 9 | do not plan | did not plan | Narrative past tense kept throughout the memory ('I taught/thought'). 'I do not plan' is a tense shift. |
| 10 | taught | thought | Confusable verbs: 'teach, taught' and 'think, thought'. |
| 11 | will be | would be | Sequence of tenses: 'would' after the past verb 'thought'. |
| 12 | shear | share | Spelling and meaning: 'shear' means to cut wool; one 'shares' an experience. |
| 13 | belief | believe | 'Belief' is the noun, 'believe' the verb needed after 'I'. |
| 14 | or by my sharing may help | and that my sharing may help | Two clauses after 'believe' are joined by 'and that'; 'or by' breaks the grammar. |
| 15 | evolved | passed | Hours 'pass'; 'evolve' means develop gradually. |
| 16 | in day | during the day | Fixed expression with the article: 'during the day'. |
| 17 | exausted | exhausted | Spelling of 'exhausted'. |
| 18 | dead | death | 'Dead' is an adjective; the noun is 'death'. |
| 19 | the hard thing | the hardest thing | Superlative needed with 'ever' ('the hardest thing I have ever...'). |
| 20 | I ever have to deal with | I have ever had to deal with | Present perfect with 'ever' for life experience: 'have ever had to'. |
| 21 | formular | formula | Spelling of 'formula'. |
| 22 | overwhelmed | overwhelming | Participle adjective: the emotions are 'overwhelming' (they overwhelm); 'overwhelmed' describes the person. |
| 23 | am | was | Tense consistency with 'I was supposed'. |
| 24 | how I was supposed to say | what I was supposed to say | 'How' cannot introduce the content of speech: use 'what'. |
| 25 | adrifted | adrift | 'Adrift' is the adjective (floating without direction); there is no verb 'adrift'. |
| 26 | loss love | lost love | Past participle used as an adjective: 'lost love'. |
| 27 | loose life | lost life | 'Loose' (not tight) is confused with 'lost' (past participle of 'lose'). |
| 28 | This powerless | This powerlessness | A noun is needed after the demonstrative 'This'. |
| 29 | reflect | reflects | Subject-verb agreement: 'This powerlessness ... reflects' (singular). |

**Marking (indicative; the paper prints 15 marks for the question but not their split)**

About half a mark for each fault identified AND correctly corrected, up to 15 marks; the corrected text must be copied in full with the corrections underlined (in your answer booklet, underline each corrected word or group of words). A change that introduces a new error earns nothing. Other acceptable corrections exist for some faults (for example 'in the day' for 'during the day', 'passed by' for 'passed', 'the news struck me like a blow to the head' for the idiom).

**Common mistakes**

1. Correcting the visible spelling mistakes only and missing the grammar faults (tense, agreement, word class).
2. Rewriting whole sentences instead of correcting the faults, so that the corrections cannot be marked.
3. Forgetting to copy the whole corrected text or to underline the corrections.
